summary: This project transforms technical telemetry and archival records of discarded NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars into an engaging, 20-slide interactive planetary storybook. Rather than viewing lunar descent stages, rovers, and landers as "space junk," our presentation gives 9 iconic spacecraft first-person voices—allowing learners of all ages to explore their exact coordinates, mission lifespans, and cosmic heritage.
details: The Challenge Over six decades of space exploration, more than 225 tons of human hardware across 80+ sites have been left behind on the Moon and Mars. To the general public and younger students, these remnants are often dismissed as "space debris" or buried in dense scientific catalogs, obscuring their historic value and lessons for planetary sustainability. Our Solution: An Interactive Planetary Storybook We designed Abandoned but not Forgotten as a visual, narrative-driven presentation structured into three chapters: Chapter 1 — Silent Sentinels of the Moon: First-person chronicles from Apollo 11 Eagle, Apollo 15 Moon Buggy, Surveyor 3, and Apollo 17 Challenger, alongside a six-decade timeline of lunar exploration. Chapter 2 — Pioneers of the Red Planet: Personal stories and longevity comparisons from Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and the Ingenuity Helicopter. Chapter 3 — Planetary Stewardship: Explores how NASA heritage guidelines, off-world material science, and future resource recycling protect cosmic history while enabling sustainable Artemis-era exploration. How We Built It We curated verified landing coordinates, mission durations, and archival imagery from NASA open repositories and synthesized them into a clean, dual-deck presentation system—featuring a concise 7-slide Project Demo for judges and a 20-slide Full Presentation for classroom and public storytelling.
